simple.meaning: זִקְנָה (ziqnâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “old age.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: זִקְנָה (H2209) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 24:36, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Kings, Psalms, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זִקְנָה (H2209) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in זִקְנָה (H2209) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: זִקְנָה (ziqnâh) / H2209 is traced through Genesis 24:36, 1 Kings 11:4, 1 Kings 15:23, Psalms 71:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.

majorEvents.evidenceText: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.

timeline.evidenceText: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned away his heart after other gods; and his heart was not perfect with Yahweh his God, as the heart of David his father was.

Now the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
Don’t reject me in my old age.
Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don’t forsake me,
Even to old age I am he,
